study type: Animal model (in vitro observation of isolated tissue)
exposure: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) model induced by prenatal testosterone exposure
outcome: Uterine contractions (irregularity, frequency, resting tone, amplitude of rhythmic contractions)
cohort: Isolated uterine tissues from adult female offspring of rats, where mothers in the experimental group received 5 mg of free testosterone on gestational day 20 and controls received solvent.
finding: PCOS rats (from mothers exposed to prenatal testosterone) showed more irregular uterine contractions compared to controls, specifically exhibiting significantly increased frequency and resting tone after exposure to carbachol.
followup_time: N/A (observations were taken in adulthood of the offspring, but specific time is not given)
gest_age: N/A (Maternal exposure was on gestational day 20, but the gestational age of the offspring at birth is not specified).
